disclaimer: This page helps you count ordinary notice dates under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006. It is not legal advice and it does not file a notice for you. Use the official Form N9 from Tribunals Ontario, and read the instructions on that form.

sources.name: Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, S.O. 2006, c. 17, sections 2 (1), 16, 38, 44, 47, 191 and 193
sources.note: Official e-Laws text, read on 2026-11-19, America/Toronto. Section 2 (1) defines the Rules as the Board's rules of practice and procedure. Section 44 sets the 28 and 60 day periods and the February and March rule. Section 47 lets a tenant end a tenancy at the end of a period or term by notice under s. 44. Section 191 (1) lists how a notice is given, and clause (g) adds any other means allowed in the Rules. Section 191 (3) says mail counts on the fifth day after mailing. Section 38 (1) turns an ended fixed term into a monthly tenancy. Section 16 gives a person who claims an amount after a breach a duty to take reasonable steps to minimize losses, mentioned beside the late rent estimate. Section 193 says time is computed under the Rules. Section 44 (5) is quoted word for word in february_march_rule.statute_text, read on 19 November 2026 through the e-Laws document service.

sources.name: Legislation Act, 2006, S.O. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, sections 87, 88, 89 (1) and 89 (3)
sources.note: Section 87 says a holiday is a holiday as described in s. 88. Section 88 (2) lists Sunday and Ontario's named holidays, used for courier timing. Section 89 (1) extends a time limit that would expire on a holiday to include the next day that is not a holiday, which the author reads as applying to the January 1 and February 1 deadlines in s. 44 (5); the page shows that later day only as the author's reading. Section 89 (3) says how days are counted: the day notice is given is left out and the termination day is counted, even when a rule says at least. Read on 2026-11-19, America/Toronto.

sources.name: Landlord and Tenant Board, Form N9: Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy (v. 01/04/2022), important information pages
sources.note: Every field the tenant or representative must complete is on pages 1 and 3. The Office Use Only box on page 3 is for the Board. PDF returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-19, America/Toronto.

sources.name: Landlord and Tenant Board Rules of Procedure, rules 1.1, 1.14, 1.15, 3.1, 3.5 and 3.9
sources.note: Rule 1.1 defines a holiday as any Saturday, Sunday or other day the Board's offices are closed. Rule 1.14 lets a thing whose time ends on a holiday be done on the next day that is not a holiday; the page names that day and does not rely on it. Rule 1.15 says a notice or document may be delivered to a party or person on a holiday and a notice may take effect on a holiday. Rule 3.1 allows service by courier, and by email if the person receiving it has consented in writing, in addition to the methods in the Act. Rule 3.5 says parties may consent in writing at any time to service by email, and rule 3.6 says that consent may be revoked in writing. Rule 3.9: courier counts the day after it was given to the courier, or if that day is a holiday the next day that is not a holiday; email counts the day it was sent; hand delivery the day it was given. Read on 2026-11-19, America/Toronto.

sources.name: Canada Post official holiday schedule
sources.note: Read on 19 November 2026, America/Toronto. The page lists official 2026 and 2027 dates, including Boxing Day (National) on December 28 in both years, and says there is no collection or delivery of mail on national, provincial and territorial holidays. It also says post offices operated by the private sector are open according to the hours of the host business, and: "When a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it may be applied to the next business day." The page gives no general weekend hours, so this page simply does not count a Saturday or Sunday as a mailing day and advises a dated receipt. Regular collection and delivery occur on provincial Family Day holidays. Years after 2027 are computed from the same holiday names with that weekend rule, not copied from a published table. The calendar is used only for the advised mail send day, not for when notice legally counts under s. 191 (3). Years 2028 to 2035 are calculated by this page, not published by Canada Post.

ordinary_rules.label: Monthly tenancy
ordinary_rules.summary: Give at least 60 days' notice. The termination date must be the last day of a rental period. If you pay on the first day of each month, that is usually the last day of the month.

ordinary_rules.label: Weekly tenancy
ordinary_rules.summary: Give at least 28 days' notice. The termination date must be the last day of a rental period. If you pay each Monday, the instructions say the termination date must be a Sunday.

ordinary_rules.label: Daily tenancy
ordinary_rules.summary: Give at least 28 days' notice. The termination date must be the last day of a rental period.

ordinary_rules.label: Fixed-term tenancy (for example a one-year lease)
ordinary_rules.summary: Give at least 60 days' notice, to be effective on the expiration date in the agreement. The termination date cannot be earlier than the last date of the fixed term, unless a listed exception on the official form applies.

february_march_rule.summary: When the tenant would normally have to give 60 days' notice, a notice for the last day of February may be given no later than January 1 of that year, and a notice for the last day of March may be given no later than February 1 of that year. The official N9 instructions describe this as a special rule that allows less than 60 days' notice in those two cases. This page advises giving notice by the literal January 1 or February 1 date, and when a notice only reaches the end of February or March on the reading below, the headline end date is the later one that meets the literal date. On the author's reading of Legislation Act s. 89 (1), a deadline that falls on a Sunday or an s. 88 holiday runs to the next day that is neither, so January 1 runs to January 2 or later, and a February 1 that falls on a Sunday runs to the Monday. No tribunal or court decision applying s. 89 (1) to these dates is cited, so the later day is shown only as a possible limit. LTB rule 1.15 lets a notice be delivered on a holiday.
february_march_rule.statute_text: (5) A tenant who gives notice under subsection (2), (3) or (4) which specifies that the termination is to be effective on the last day of February or the last day of March in any year shall be deemed to have given at least 60 days notice of termination if the notice is given not later than January 1 of that year in respect of a termination which is to be effective on the last day of February, or February 1 of that year in respect of a termination which is to be effective on the last day of March. 2006, c. 17, s. 44 (5).
february_march_rule.statute_text_source: Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 44 (5), official e-Laws text read on 19 November 2026, America/Toronto.
february_march_rule.scope: Subsection (2) is a monthly tenancy, (3) a yearly tenancy and (4) a fixed term. So the engine applies s. 44 (5) to monthly tenancies and to fixed terms whose expiry date is the last day of February or the last day of March, and never to daily or weekly tenancies under s. 44 (1).
february_march_rule.deeming_note: Section 44 (5) is a deeming rule, not a time limit: notice given by January 1 or February 1 is treated as at least 60 days. Legislation Act s. 89 (1) speaks of time limits that would otherwise expire on a holiday, so the deeming wording makes the author's s. 89 (1) reading weaker still. That is why the headline end date, the Form N9 checklist and the calendar reminder always use the literal date, and an end date that needs the reading is shown only as a contingent line.

exceptions_not_calculated: If the landlord was required to use the standard form of lease, did not, and you made a written demand, the N9 instructions describe a limited way to end a fixed term earlier. This tool does not try to date that path.

If the landlord has given you an N12 or N13 notice, the N9 instructions allow a termination date 10 days or more after you give N9, and it does not have to be the last day of a period. This tool does not date that path.
If the landlord refused a request to assign the unit, the instructions set a 30-day or 28-day path that does not have to land on a period end. This tool does not date that path.
Care-home rules and the 28-day path for tenants who have experienced sexual or domestic violence use different Board forms and are not calculated here. See Tribunals Ontario for those forms.

delivery_rules.deemed: the day after hand off, or the next day that is not a holiday: not a Saturday, Sunday or Legislation Act s. 88 holiday, and not Civic Holiday, which is treated as a possible office closure
delivery_rules.source: RTA s. 191 (1) (g); LTB Rules 1.1, 3.1 and 3.9; Legislation Act, 2006, s. 88

counting_rule: Days are counted the way the Legislation Act, 2006, s. 89 (3) says: leave out the day notice is given and count the termination day. Notice given on May 1 reaches June 30 with exactly 60 days.
limits: Courier and email timing rely on RTA s. 191 (1) (g) and LTB rules 3.1, 3.5, 3.6 and 3.9, which are written mainly for Board matters. See service_chain for the reading used.

Under LTB rule 1.1 a weekday is a holiday only if the Board's offices are closed. No Board closure calendar was found, so the s. 88 holidays, Civic Holiday and Boxing Day observed on December 28 are labelled UNKNOWN and counted as closed, and the page says when that changes a date.

The January 1 and February 1 deadlines in s. 44 (5) are fixed dates. The advised send day always meets the literal date. On the author's reading of Legislation Act s. 89 (1), a deadline that falls on a Sunday or an s. 88 holiday extends to the next day that is neither, and the page shows that later day only as the author's reading. The official text, read on 19 November 2026 from e-Laws, says: s. 89 (1) "Time limits that would otherwise expire on a holiday are extended to include the next day that is not a holiday." Section 87 says holiday means a holiday as described in section 88, and s. 88 (2) lists Sunday and the named holidays. Section 46 says "Every provision of this Part applies to every Act and regulation." On that reading January 1, 2027 becomes Saturday, January 2, 2027. RTA s. 193 and LTB rule 1.14 could be read to reach the next weekday as well, for example Monday, January 4, 2027. The page names that day and does not rely on it. LTB rule 1.15 says a notice may be delivered on a holiday, so giving notice on January 1 itself needs no extension. The 60 day and 28 day minimum periods are not extended, because they are minimum notice periods rather than time limits that expire. No tribunal or court decision applying s. 89 (1) to these dates is cited. That is the author's reading, not an adjudicated interpretation.
A day fixed as a holiday by proclamation, or an unplanned office closure, is not known ahead.

service_chain.summary: How courier and email reach a tenant's notice. The Act lists hand delivery, the landlord's employee, the mail box and Canada Post in s. 191 (1) (a) to (f). Clause (g) adds any other means allowed in the Rules, and s. 2 (1) says the Rules are the Board's rules of practice and procedure. Rule 3.1 is the Rule that allows courier, and email with written consent. Rule 3.5 is how that consent is given, and rule 3.6 is how it is taken back. Rule 3.9 says on which day each method counts. Rule 1.1 says what a holiday is.

assumptions: Rule 3 is headed Service of Documents on a Person or Party and is written mainly for Board matters. This page reads rule 3.1 as one of the means allowed in the Rules under s. 191 (1) (g) for a tenant's notice given before any application. The Act does not say that in so many words, and the Board could read it differently.

A landlord's written consent to email is taken to cover Form N9 only if it says so. The Board's consent form does not list a tenant's notice to end the tenancy, and consent can be revoked under rule 3.6.
Hand delivery, the mail box and Canada Post come straight from s. 191 (1) and (3) and do not depend on the Rules. When the date matters most, those are the safer methods.

holiday_kinds.weekend: Saturday and Sunday, named in LTB rule 1.1 itself. These are the only skipped days that do not depend on an assumption.
holiday_kinds.statutory: Listed in the Legislation Act, 2006, s. 88 (2), with the extra days in s. 88 (3) (the Monday after a New Year's Day that falls on a Sunday), s. 88 (4) (Canada Day moves to July 2 when July 1 is a Sunday) and s. 88 (5) (the Monday after a Christmas Day on a Saturday, the Tuesday after one on a Sunday). Rule 1.1 does not use the s. 88 list. It counts a weekday as a holiday only if the Board's offices are closed, so each of these is labelled UNKNOWN and counted as a closure. The Board does not publish a closure calendar that this page could find.
holiday_kinds.assumed: Civic Holiday, and December 28 when Boxing Day falls on a Saturday or Sunday (Boxing Day observed, listed by Canada Post as a holiday with no collection or delivery). Neither is on the s. 88 list. Both are labelled UNKNOWN and counted as a closure, for the same reason.
holiday_kinds.effect: For the weekdays this page lists (the s. 88 holidays, Civic Holiday and Boxing Day observed), counting a day as closed can only make a courier notice count later and the advised send day earlier, never later. The list does not include every possible closure. When an assumption alone changes the end date, the page says what the date would be if the offices were open.
holiday_kinds.unknown: A day fixed by proclamation, or an unplanned office closure, cannot be known ahead. Leave a spare day.

n9_scope: Every field the tenant or representative must complete. The Office Use Only box is left out. The page does not fill in, sign or send the form.

published.note: Copied from the Canada Post official holiday schedule page, read on 19 November 2026, America/Toronto. Each row in site/dates.js has published: true.

calculated.note: Computed by this page from the holiday names and the weekend rule on that page. Canada Post has not published or confirmed these years in any schedule this page has read. Each row has published: false, and the tests check the two groups separately. When an advised mailing day depends on a calculated year, the page says so.

canada_post_schedule.collection: The schedule lists holidays with no collection or delivery of mail. It does not promise weekend collection, and a post office inside a store keeps the store's hours. A theoretical last mailing day on a weekend or holiday is therefore not a day with confirmed collection. A dated counter receipt is evidence of the mailing day, not proof of how the Board will count it.
